note: The World Inequality Database (WID.world, bulk download of 15 October 2026, read again in that of 30 October 2026), Republic of the Congo, 2024: average net personal wealth (ahweal992j) and average post-tax national income (adiinc992j) per adult over 20, resources split equally within couples, in XAF of that year, for the bottom 20, 40, 60, 90 and 99 percent and the top 1 percent; each family's band is read from them. Read 2026-10-30. Read again 2026-11-03 from the bulk download of 30 October 2026 (its country files dated 30 October 2026): every row quoted here, its year and its currency label stood as before, and no later year was given. Until 2026-11-03 this note and its sources wrote the variable codes with their age and population parts swapped (ahwealj992 for ahweal992j and adiincj992 for adiinc992j), codes no file of the database holds (its README: type, concept, age group, population, as in sptinc992j), and called adiinc992j post-tax disposable income, which its metadata names post-tax national income ([Post-tax national income]=[Post-tax disposable income]+[Public spending]). The national accounts (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-03: each band's income scaled by households' disposable income over national income), searched again on 2026-11-03 in the statistics office's own accounts for a households' disposable income account from 2019 on, found none: INS Congo publications API (ins-congo.cg/backend/api/publications/list.php?sous_secteur=comptes-nationaux), read 2026-11-03: 14 records; annual reports for 2005-2018, 2019, provisional 2020, 2021 and definitive 2022, plus quarterly accounts to Q4 2025. INS Congo, Comptes nationaux définitifs 2022 (PDF, 24 pages, and its workbook uploads/publications/ins_6a84134a124846.56446583.xlsx, Tables 1-15), read 2026-11-03: resources-and-uses balance, aggregates 2018-2022 (GDP, output, intermediate consumption, value added, final consumption, GFCF, trade), GDP by branch and by use. No national income, no disposable income, no sector accounts. The 2021 and provisional 2020 reports hold the same plan. BEAC economic database for Congo (beac.int/wp-content/uploads/2016/10/deor_congo.xlsx, resources and uses), read 2026-11-03: private consumption is given for enterprises and households together; no household account. Each band's income stayed the database's post-tax national income, public spending included.
